cards.title: Staying hydrated
facts: Plain water is the best drink for everyday hydration.
You need more water in hot weather and during sport.
Energy drinks contain caffeine and are not meant for children.
do: Sip through the day, not all at once
Drink more on hot days and after sport
dont: Don't use fizzy drinks to quench thirst

myths.statement: Energy drinks are a good way for kids to recover after sport.
myths.truth: They have lots of caffeine and sugar. Plain water is best after normal play.

quiz.q: You just played football for an hour on a hot afternoon. Best drink?
quiz.explanation: Plain water rehydrates best. Other drinks add a lot of sugar.

cards.title: Reading food labels
facts: Ingredients are listed from most to least.
'No added sugar' doesn't mean no sugar.
Nutrition values are often given per serving, not per pack.

myths.statement: A label saying 'no added sugar' means the food has no sugar.
myths.truth: It can still contain natural sugars, sometimes a lot. Check the sugar line.

myths.statement: Ingredients on a label are listed from the largest amount to the smallest.
myths.truth: The first ingredient is what the food contains most of.

quiz.q: On a food label, ingredients are listed…
quiz.explanation: The first ingredients make up most of the product.

situations: {At}, {name} is choosing a snack. One packet says 'Multigrain! Baked!' in big letters, but the label lists sugar and refined flour first. {relation} says the slogan means it's healthy.
scenario.question: How should {name} decide which snack is the better choice?

rubric.point: Read the ingredients list, not the slogan
rubric.note: Ingredients are listed from most to least.

rubric.point: Check sugar and salt per serving
Prefer fruit, nuts or roasted snacks as a better swap

cards.title: A balanced tiffin
facts: A balanced meal includes vegetables or fruit, whole grains and a protein.
Different coloured vegetables give different nutrients.
do: Fill half the plate with vegetables and fruit
Add a protein like dal, eggs, paneer, curd or sprouts
Choose whole grains like roti, brown rice or millets
dont: Don't make packaged snacks the main meal

myths.statement: Skipping breakfast helps you concentrate better at school.
myths.truth: Breakfast gives energy for the morning. Skipping it can make concentrating harder.

quiz.q: Which tiffin is the most balanced?
options: Roti, dal, cucumber and an apple

cards.title: Food hygiene
facts: Washing hands with soap for 20 seconds removes most germs.
Cooked food left uncovered attracts flies and germs.
do: Wash hands with soap before eating
dont: Don't eat food left uncovered for long
Don't share half-eaten food or bottles when sick

myths.statement: Rinsing hands with water alone is as good as washing with soap.
myths.truth: Soap helps lift germs off the skin. Wash for about 20 seconds.

quiz.q: How long should you wash hands with soap?
quiz.explanation: About 20 seconds, the time it takes to hum 'Happy Birthday' twice.
